goal: Build Codex Widget into a durable local-first desktop product with daemon-owned state, recoverable sessions, artifact history, and extensible provider/theme foundations.
newUserRequests: Route all follow-up work through the vibe-iterate workflow instead of one-off UI or feature patches.
Introduce a daemon-owned SQLite storage layer after reviewing project structure and future data needs.
Support multiple internal conversation tabs, session restore after app restart, session trash, and branch-to-new-session behavior.
Preserve generated, modified, and deleted files through an artifact ledger with versions and reusable viewers in chat and trash.
Let Vision choose between WebM screen recording and Agent screen streaming, with future voice prompt and interactive screen-sharing sessions in mind.
Keep renderer focused on UI and interaction while daemon owns sessions, messages, app-server runtime, provider snapshots, artifacts, and activity logs.
carryoverSummary: Iteration 2 completed the app-server runtime, reconnect replay, regenerate rollback, DOM/Vision/PTY providers, renderer chat hardening, release readiness gates, and resident desktop operations for dogfooding.
Visible chat persistence is still renderer localStorage-based; durable product state now needs a daemon-owned storage authority.
Branching currently uses one-shot branch context and runtime reset; the next target is an internal tab/session model.
Provider snapshots, terminal output, activity detail, and generated file artifacts are not yet modeled as durable first-class entities.
Browser store account submission remains deferred until after dogfooding and is not part of this iteration's implementation scope.
openRisks: Codex app-server protocol remains experimental; keep exec fallback and avoid assuming thread resume across app restarts.
SQLite must not store OAuth or Codex credentials; secrets stay in the existing auth boundary.
Large artifacts, screenshots, and recordings should use blob files with DB metadata to avoid bloating SQLite.
Screen streaming and recording need explicit CPU, memory, and retention limits before daily dogfooding.
